probe: docker image label + on-image file read (no container from the measurement run survived; the image did)
why: M17/M18/M19 measure MongoDB search freshness. They were run against the mongodb/mongodb-atlas-local image. Until the mongot build inside that image was identified, those three measurements carried an unnamed reserve: 'some mongot'. This pins it.

commit_interval.note: NOT established. The commit/refresh interval is not exposed in /opt/mongot/mongot (launch script), in /opt/mongot/README.md, or as an image environment variable. It is internal to the mongot jar. The ~1015 ms figure of M17 and the de-synchronised distribution of M18 remain EMPIRICAL observations of this build's behaviour, not a read of a documented default.

consequence.severity: raises the reserve on M17, M18 and M19 rather than lowering it
consequence.statement: mongot here is the localDev edition, which MongoDB ships for local development, not the search tier that serves Atlas. Therefore the measured write-to-searchable lag is a property of mongot 1.75.1 localDev running beside a single-node replica set on a loaded shared host. It may NOT be quoted as 'MongoDB Atlas Search lag', as 'MongoDB's search freshness', or as a property of MongoDB the product.

does_not_affect.direction: The DIRECTION survives: mongot indexes asynchronously off the change stream by construction, so a just-written document is not immediately searchable, whereas HCD's SAI/JVector is on the write path. That is an architectural difference, not a build artefact.
does_not_affect.hcd_side: The HCD half of those measurements (M7, findings_hcd_vec_freshness.json) is unaffected; it carries its own separate reserve, that 'synchronous' was only ever bounded below the ~45 ms HTTP floor, never shown to be zero.

consequence.what_would_close_it: Repeat M17/M18/M19 against a production-edition mongot (Atlas, or a deployment whose /etc/mongodb-atlas-local/mongot-edition is not localDev) and compare the lag distributions. Not possible on this host.
